name: superpowers-trae
description: Professional AI development skills for Trae IDE: TDD, systematic debugging, brainstorming, code review, and proven engineering workflows

skills.name: brainstorming
skills.description: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes. Four phases: Root Cause Investigation → Pattern Analysis → Hypothesis and Testing → Implementation.

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code. Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

skills.name: writing-plans
skills.description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code. Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context.

skills.name: executing-plans
skills.description: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints.

skills.name: subagent-driven-development
skills.description: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session. Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims.

skills.name: requesting-code-review
skills.description: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements.

skills.name: receiving-code-review
skills.description: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable.

skills.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
skills.description: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies.

skills.name: using-git-worktrees
skills.description: Use when starting any new development work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans.

skills.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skills.description: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work.

skills.name: writing-skills
skills.description: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment.

skills.name: using-superpowers
skills.description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring Skill tool invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions.
